name: Cathedral Basilica of Potosí
scope: The standing nineteenth-century cathedral on the north side of Plaza 10 de Noviembre in Potosí.
era: Present exterior of the cathedral dedicated in 1836 with paired octagonal towers recorded in 1908.

stories.title: The Cathedral That Rose From Its Own Collapse

externalReferences.artist: International Bureau of the American Republics (publisher)

originalReview.notes: The original leaf labels the cathedral in Potosí and depicts the two octagonal belfries, central curved stone front and side roofline. The original Washington, DC cover dates the issue to September 1908.

review.method: Exactly matched public-domain originals, native building footprint and published architectural dimensions.
review.notes: Started with the published Qualla gallery. The hero’s date and origin were uncertain and the 1758 drawing represents the predecessor. The exact 1908 published photograph had a documented original leaf and dated issue cover.
